data.narrative:
Isembard is a Series A-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a peer set of five same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables drawn from a broader universe of nine private companies and one public company (277810.KQ) in robotics and manufacturing. The peer median valuation stands at $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

Two valuation methods triangulate the assessment. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for base value ($400M), applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, yielding $800M. Peer-median analysis across the five-company comparable set directly implies $1.6B. These methods produce a low bound of $680M and a high bound of $1.9B, with a triangulated median of $1.2B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $680M to $1.9B, centered on $1.2B. Key uncertainties include stage-specific calibration within the peer set—the comparables span from Seed through Series B—and the limited public market data available for robotics. The relative stability of the two methods around the $1.2B-$1.6B band provides modest confidence in that zone, though execution risk and downstream fundraising conditions remain material drivers.
